description:
Perfect Sugar-free Hibiscus Sorbet in the Ninja Creami:

Discover how to create the perfect sugar-free hibiscus sorbet using the Ninja Creami! 🌺 This vibrant, tangy, and refreshing hibiscus sorbet is made with just a few simple ingredients, making it perfect for anyone craving a guilt-free treat. Whether you’re following a sugar-free diet or simply looking for a healthy dessert option, this hibiscus sorbet is perfect in every way.

In this video, I’ll walk you through the entire process—from steeping hibiscus flowers for maximum flavor to achieving that silky-smooth sorbet texture in the Ninja Creami. Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more delicious recipes! 🍨

-----------

🕒 Timestamps
0:00 – Introduction to Sugar-Free Hibiscus Sorbet
0:16 – Ingredients You’ll Need
1:08 – Combining Ingredients
3:51 – Sorbet Specs
4:44 – The FLAT TOP Ninja Creami tubs should have!
5:14 – Scoopy Scoop
5:31 – Final Taste Test
5:53 – Outro: Share Your Creations!

-------------

Ingredients:
 • Dried hibiscus flowers
 • Xylitol (allulose also works)
 • Inulin
 • Water

---------------

Why You’ll Love This Recipe:
✔️ Sugar-free & diabetic-friendly
✔️ Bursting with natural hibiscus flavor
✔️ Made effortlessly in the Ninja Creami
✔️ Healthy, vibrant, and absolutely delicious

If you enjoyed this recipe, make sure to check out my other sugar-free and Ninja Creami recipes on the channel. 💡 Got a request for a specific recipe? Let me know in the comments below!

🎥 Subscribe for more: [Insert channel link]
📸 Follow me on Instagram for behind-the-scenes: [Insert Instagram handle]

#SugarFreeSorbet #HibiscusDessert #NinjaCreamiRecipes #HealthyDessert #SorbetRecipe

Enjoy your sugar-free hibiscus sorbet adventure! 🌺✨

comments.text:
A jamaica keto sorbet! I can't wait to try this in the Creami I got for Christmas! Thank you!

I'm from Arizona. At least here, dried hibiscus flowers are sold in any Latino market as flor de jamaica. I've made the drink many times, but never attempted it with a non-sugar sweetener.

Your notes said you can sub allulose for xylitol. I can't handle the sugar alcohols--none of them, no matter how small the quantity. Even those naturally occuring in fruits like the sorbitol in apples makes me sick. So I need to sub in the allulose. Does the weight stay the same as for xylitol?

comments.text: Great vid - just got a Creami and am exploring the "right" way to make gelato, ice cream and sorbets. Have an idea about making sorbet using Bickfords Bitter Lemon cordial (10-12% sugar) as the base flavour. Looks like I can use the inulin to bump up solids and then balance the sugar out to 25-35% with adding some water to the cordial and topping up the sugars. Thoughts? BTW, would love to see how you get rid of the Mt Creami bump. Cheers from Oz!
comments.author: @HenkPlaggemars

comments.text:
Absolutely, great idea to use flavors around the house you like. Just watch the strength of the cordial as they can be super strong and overpowering. 
I’ll do a video on it soon.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  Worked really well - nice clean citrus flavour, although a little sloppy after 1 spin on the Sorbet setting (Creami Deluxe). Used Xylitol as the sugar to add to the cordial sugar and bring it up to ~28%. Diluted the cordial 1:4 with water and added in some inulin as per your recipe here (scaled down for 700 mL). Used Guar gum as the stabilizer - had half a lime sitting on the bench and squeezed that in too. Have it in the freezer now to firm up and see if the texture improves - I'll post again after its had some time...
comments.author: @HenkPlaggemars

comments.text: Definitely improved with freezing. Plan to reduce sugar (xylitol) next time and maybe add some lime zest to spruce it up even further.
comments.author: @HenkPlaggemars

comments.text:
Do you think insulating the sides of the Creami tub while freezing would prevent the bump in unbalanced recipes?

Perhaps allowing the sides to cool slower would allow it to freeze from bottom to top evenly.
comments.author: @shinjincai

comments.text: I doubt it, it’s caused by too much water expanding during the freezing process.
